descriptor: Adobe's design system (Spectrum 2), token + schema driven

sections.overview:
### Overview
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/

Adobe **Spectrum** is Adobe's design system; **Spectrum 2 (S2)** is the current generation. Its public, machine-readable core is **Spectrum Design Data** — design tokens, component API schemas, a terminology registry, and guideline documents — published open source, alongside a **draft Design Data Specification** (v1.0.0-draft).

### What ships
- **Design tokens** — color, typography, and layout, resolvable by mode (`light`/`dark`/`wireframe`) and platform scale (`desktop`/`mobile`).
- **Component schemas** — 98 components with machine-readable API (properties, types, defaults), state model, and anatomy.
- **Registry** — canonical vocabulary for sizes, states, variants, and glossary.
- **Guideline documents** — standalone JSON pages (principles, colors, spacing, motion, etc.) with typed `documentBlocks` (purpose, guideline, do-dont, examples).

### Implementations
- **React Spectrum** + **React Aria** (behavior/a11y), **Spectrum Web Components**, and `@adobe/spectrum-tokens`.

### Value abstraction
Spectrum resolves values behind **named tokens**; the same token adapts across mode and platform. Prefer token names; published raw values are given where available below.

### Known gaps
- Design Data Specification is **Draft** — schemas and normative text may change before 1.0.0.
- Current `@adobe/spectrum-tokens` JSON uses the legacy shape (`color-set`, `scale-set`); the DTCG-aligned target format and migration are in progress (repo #723).
sections.colors:
### Colors
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/tokens/color-palette/

Color is layered: a **raw palette** (`color-palette`), a **semantic palette** (`semantic-color-palette`, e.g. `accent-color-*` aliasing `blue-*`), **color aliases** (`color-aliases`), and **component color** tokens. Every color token is a `color-set` resolving per mode: `light`, `dark`, `wireframe`. The S2 palette was regenerated with the **Leonardo** tool and tuned to be more color-vision-deficiency-safe and to include Adobe brand colors.

### Grays (Spectrum 2 = 13 grays)
S2 added `gray-25` and `gray-1000` and made **gray-25 the default background** (brighter, higher contrast than S1's gray-100).

| Token | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gray-25` (`background-base-color`) | rgb(255, 255, 255) | rgb(17, 17, 17) |
| `gray-50` | rgb(248, 248, 248) | rgb(27, 27, 27) |
| `gray-100` | rgb(233, 233, 233) | rgb(44, 44, 44) |
| `gray-200` | rgb(225, 225, 225) | rgb(50, 50, 50) |
| `gray-500` | rgb(143, 143, 143) | rgb(109, 109, 109) |
| `gray-800` | rgb(41, 41, 41) | rgb(219, 219, 219) |
| `gray-900` | rgb(19, 19, 19) | rgb(242, 242, 242) |
| `gray-1000` | rgb(0, 0, 0) | rgb(255, 255, 255) |

### Accent (semantic → blue)
| Token | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accent-color-900` (`{blue-900}`) | rgb(59, 99, 251) | rgb(86, 129, 255) |
| `accent-color-1000` (`{blue-1000}`) | rgb(39, 77, 234) | rgb(105, 149, 254) |
| `negative-color-1000` (`{red-1000}`) | rgb(183, 40, 24) | rgb(255, 103, 86) |

### Background layers
- **`background-base-color`** (`{gray-25}`): base page background.
- **`background-layer-1-color`** (`{gray-50}`): raised layer.
- **`background-layer-2-color`**: canvas layer — light rgb(255, 255, 255), dark rgb(34, 34, 34).

### Known gaps
- Full palette (all hues × 16 stops × 3 modes) is large; only representative real values shown — see source for the complete set.
- Data-visualization color values are noted by Spectrum as **not yet published** in the token set (see Data Visualization).
sections.typography:
### Typography
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/tokens/typography/

Font families (real token values): sans **`Adobe Clean Spectrum VF`** (`sans-serif-font-family`), serif **`Adobe Clean Serif`**, CJK **`Adobe Clean Han`**, code **`Source Code Pro`**. Weights (`font-weight` tokens): `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `bold`, `extra-bold`, `black`. `letter-spacing` = `0em`; line-height multipliers `line-height-100` = 1.3, `line-height-200` = 1.5.

### Font size scale (`scale-set`, desktop / mobile)
| Token | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font-size-25` | 10px | 12px |
| `font-size-50` | 11px | 13px |
| `font-size-75` | 12px | 15px |
| `font-size-100` (base) | 14px | 17px |
| `font-size-200` | 16px | 19px |
| `font-size-300` | 18px | 22px |
| `font-size-400` | 20px | 24px |
| `font-size-500` | 22px | 27px |
| `font-size-600` | 25px | 31px |
| `font-size-700` | 28px | 34px |
| `font-size-800` | 32px | 39px |
| `font-size-900` | 36px | 44px |
| `font-size-1000` | 40px | 49px |
| `font-size-1100` | 45px | 55px |
| `font-size-1200` | 51px | 62px |
| `font-size-1300` | 58px | 70px |
| `font-size-1400` | 65px | 79px |
| `font-size-1500` | 73px | 88px |

### T-shirt scales (React Spectrum `font` style macro)
> Source: https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/style-macro
Six type scales, each with a default + t-shirt modifiers: **UI** (`ui-xs`…`ui-3xl`), **Body** (`body-2xs`…`body-3xl`), **Heading** (`heading-2xs`…`heading-3xl`), **Title** (`title-xs`…`title-3xl`), **Detail** (`detail-sm`…`detail-xl`), **Code** (`code-xs`…`code-xl`). The `font` shorthand sets `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, and `color` together (e.g. `font: 'heading-xl'`). Base is a 14px, and sizes scale up ~1.25× on touch devices.

### Known gaps
- Semantic scale tokens (`body-size-*`, `heading-size-*`) alias the `font-size-*` set — see source for the full alias map.
- Detailed per-size line-heights are published as `line-height-font-size-*` scale-sets in the source.
sections.layout:
### Layout
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/tokens/layout/

Layout primitives are `dimension` (fixed px) or `scale-set` (desktop/mobile). Layout is token-driven, not hardcoded.

### Spacing scale (`spacing-*`, `dimension`)
| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `spacing-25` | 1px |
| `spacing-50` | 2px |
| `spacing-75` | 4px |
| `spacing-85` | 6px |
| `spacing-100` | 8px |
| `spacing-200` | 12px |
| `spacing-300` | 16px |
| `spacing-350` | 20px |
| `spacing-400` | 24px |
| `spacing-500` | 32px |
| `spacing-600` | 40px |
| `spacing-700` | 48px |
| `spacing-800` | 64px |
| `spacing-900` | 80px |
| `spacing-1000` | 96px |

### Component height (`scale-set`, desktop / mobile)
| Token | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `component-height-50` | 20px | 26px |
| `component-height-75` | 24px | 30px |
| `component-height-100` | 32px | 40px |
| `component-height-200` | 40px | 50px |
| `component-height-300` | 48px | 60px |
| `component-height-400` | 56px | 70px |
| `component-height-500` | 64px | 80px |

### Other primitives
- **Border width** (`border-width-100/200/400`): 1px / 2px / 4px.
- **Base gap** (`base-gap-*`): 4–10px; **base padding** vertical/horizontal are `dimension`/`scale-set` (e.g. `base-padding-horizontal-medium` = desktop 12px / mobile 10px).
- **Focus** (`focus-indicator-thickness`): 2px.

### Spacing philosophy
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/guidelines/spacing.json
S2 uses **spacing (not dividers) as the primary way to group and divide content**; spacing values are unchanged from S1.

### Known gaps
- Component-specific layout lives in `layout-component` tokens (see source); not enumerated here.
sections.depth:
### Elevation & Depth
> Source: https://spectrum.adobe.com/page/object-styles/

S2 elevation combines **background layers** with **drop shadows**. Per Spectrum, S2 shadows are composed of **three layers — a key shadow, an ambient shadow, and a transition shadow between them**. Containers that float above content (menus, tooltips, popovers) get drop shadows to signal elevation.

### Background layers (depth without shadow)
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/guidelines/background-layers.json
- **Base**: `gray-25` — draws attention to primary content.
- **Layer 1** / **Layer 2**: successively raised surfaces (`background-layer-1-color` = `gray-50`; `background-layer-2-color` = white/light).
- Pasteboard has a dedicated background layer in editing apps.

### Drop-shadow tokens
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/tokens/layout/

| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `drop-shadow-x-100/200/300` | 0px / 0px / 0px |
| `drop-shadow-y-100/200/300` | 1px / 2px / 6px |
| `drop-shadow-blur-100/200/300` | 6px / 8px / 16px |

Semantic groupings compose these:
- **Elevated** (`drop-shadow-elevated-*`): x 0, y 2px, blur 8px.
- **Emphasized default** (`drop-shadow-emphasized-default-*`): x 0, y 1px, blur 6px; **hover**: y 2px, blur 8px.
- **Dragged** (`drop-shadow-dragged-*`): x 0, y 6px, blur 16px.

### Not published
- Per Spectrum's object-styles guideline, **detailed S2 shadow color/opacity values are "still in progress"** — only the foundational blur/offset dimensions above are published; shadow-color tokens are not exposed in `layout`.
sections.shapes:
### Shapes
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/tokens/layout/

S2 corner rounding is "more pronounced and flexible than Spectrum 1," designed so nesting a smaller object in a larger one yields a visually balanced gap.

### Corner radius scale (`corner-radius-*`, `dimension`)
| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `corner-radius-0` | 0px |
| `corner-radius-75` | 3px |
| `corner-radius-100` | 4px |
| `corner-radius-200` | 5px |
| `corner-radius-300` | 6px |
| `corner-radius-400` | 7px |
| `corner-radius-500` | 8px |
| `corner-radius-600` | 9px |
| `corner-radius-700` | 10px |
| `corner-radius-800` | 16px |
| `corner-radius-1000` | 0.5 (multiplier → full/pill) |

### Semantic radius aliases
- `corner-radius-small-default` → `{corner-radius-100}` = 4px
- `corner-radius-medium-default` → `{corner-radius-500}` = 8px
- `corner-radius-large-default` → `{corner-radius-700}` = 10px
- `corner-radius-extra-large-default` → `{corner-radius-800}` = 16px
- `corner-radius-full` → `{corner-radius-1000}` = 0.5 multiplier; `corner-radius-none` → 0px
- Size-scaled ramps exist (e.g. `corner-radius-medium-size-small/medium/large/extra-large` = 7/8/9/10px).

### Border widths
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/guidelines/object-styles.json
Two widths used in in-product UI (`border-width-100` = 1px, `border-width-200` = 2px); a 4px width (`border-width-400`) exists but is **not used in in-product UI contexts**.

### Known gaps
- Object-styles guideline notes some rounding/shadow detail is still evolving in S2.
sections.iconography:
### Iconography
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/guidelines/using-icons.json

Three icon roles: **workflow icons** (metaphors to navigate/manipulate objects), **UI icons** (atomic parts of a component — chevrons, arrows, crosses; come in assorted sizes), and **status badges** (state/presence/premium indicators). S2 switched workflow icons from **filled to an outline style**, with a single **1.5px stroke weight**, rounded inner corners (1.5px rounding), and rounded end caps.

### Workflow icon sizes (two per platform, canvas / glyph)
| Platform | Size | Canvas | Glyph (approx) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop/Web | Primary | 20px | ~18px |
| Desktop/Web | Secondary (panels, lists, cards) | 16px | ~14px |
| Mobile | Primary | 24px | ~22px |
| Mobile | Secondary | 20px | ~18px |

Icons are drawn at a 20px canvas / 1.5px stroke default; scaled to 24px mobile the stroke resolves to ~1.64px. Icons scale slightly with component size (a 20px icon is larger in a large component, smaller in a small one).

### Icon color tokens
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/tokens/icons/
Per hue and state: `icon-color-<hue>-primary-default | -hover | -down | -background` plus `icon-color-disabled-primary` (`{gray-400}`) and `icon-color-primary-default` (`{neutral-content-color-default}` = `gray-800`). Example — `icon-color-blue-primary-default`: light rgb(59, 99, 251), dark rgb(64, 105, 253).

### Not published / gaps
- `workflow-icon-size-*` scale-sets exist in `layout` tokens but are **marked deprecated**; sizing guidance above comes from the icon guideline.
- Total icon count not enumerated in the design-data set.
sections.components:
### Components
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/components/

Components are published as **machine-readable API schemas** (properties, types, defaults) plus a **state model** and **anatomy** parts. The design-data set publishes **98 component schemas**.

### Sample of published components
`accordion`, `action-bar`, `action-button`, `action-group`, `alert-banner`, `alert-dialog`, `avatar`, `avatar-group`, `badge`, `breadcrumbs`, `button`, `button-group`, `calendar`, `card`, `checkbox`, `checkbox-group`, `close-button`, `coach-mark`, `color-area`, `color-slider`, `color-wheel`, `combo-box`, `contextual-help`, `date-field`, `date-picker`, `divider`, `drop-zone`, `field-label`, `help-text`, `illustrated-message`, `link`, `list-view`, `menu`, `meter`, `number-field`, `picker`, `popover`, `progress-bar`, `progress-circle`, `radio-button`, `radio-group`, `rating`, `search-field`, `segmented-control`, `side-navigation`, `slider`, `status-light`, `steplist`, `swatch`, `switch`, `tooltip` … (98 total).

### States & anatomy (spec)
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/spec/
The spec defines a **State model** (trigger semantics, precedence/resolution, canonical state vocabulary) and **Anatomy format** (part declarations, canonical anatomy vocabulary). S2 note: some components communicate the **down state by a size change** (pressed-in illusion) rather than color; selected states default to a `gray-800` fill with an optional accent option.

### Implementation
React Spectrum + React Aria and Spectrum Web Components provide accessible implementations; the schema is the source of truth agents read.

### Known gaps
- Per-component prop tables not reproduced here — query via `design-data-component` / component pages.
sections.dataviz:
### Data Visualization
> Source: https://spectrum.adobe.com/page/color-for-data-visualization/

Spectrum publishes data-viz guidance across **Data visualization fundamentals** and **Color for data visualization**, implemented by **react-spectrum-charts** (Area/Bar/Line and more).

### Published color guidance (guidelines, not token values)
- Categorical color becomes **harder to comprehend starting at 6 colors, and extremely difficult at 12** — keep categorical palettes small.
- Use **consistent lightness across categorical hues** so viewers don't infer false rank/magnitude.
- Palettes are tuned to be **color-vision-deficiency-safe**; color is never the only encoding.

### Not published
- Per Spectrum's `colors` guideline, the **data-visualization palettes are noted as "available soon"** and are **not yet published as design tokens** in the design-data set — no categorical/sequential/diverging hex/rgb values are exposed.
- Chart-specific dimensions/spacing are defined in `react-spectrum-charts`, not the token set.

### Known gaps
- No machine-readable data-viz palette tokens yet; guidance is prose on spectrum.adobe.com.
sections.content:
### Content: Voice & Tone
> Source: https://spectrum.adobe.com/page/voice-and-tone/

Spectrum publishes UX-writing guidance on **Voice and tone**, plus system **Principles** and a **naming guide** in the machine-readable guideline set.

### Principles (machine-readable)
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/guidelines/principles.json
- **Rational** — based on real situations; every decision backed by interdisciplinary research; adaptable resources, not rigid rules.
- **Human** — puts people first; a high standard of inclusivity, accessibility, honesty, and respect; balances utility and joy.
- **Focused** — delivers what's needed when needed; every decoration purposeful; built to a high quality bar.

### Naming / terminology
> Source: https://github.com/adobe/spectrum-design-data/blob/main/SPECTRUM_NAMING_GUIDE_WIKI.md
Name things by **what the thing does** (the user's goal/task), not how it looks or behaves. Use plain-language phrases for complex, context-dependent concepts.

### Not published
- There is **no dedicated `voice-and-tone` guideline JSON** in the design-data set; the detailed voice/tone/grammar guidance lives on the spectrum.adobe.com page (client-rendered, not tokenized).
- Component-level writing guidelines are attached per component as `documentBlocks` rather than a single global doc.
sections.accessibility:
### Accessibility
> Source: https://spectrum.adobe.com/page/color-area/

Spectrum follows **WCAG 2.0 / 2.1** and states explicit criteria on component pages:
- **Text contrast** ≥ **4.5:1** small text, ≥ **3:1** large text (WCAG 1.4.3).
- **Non-text/UI contrast** ≥ **3:1** for information needed to identify components and states (WCAG 1.4.11).
- **Color is never the only means** of conveying information (WCAG 1.4.1).
- Keyboard interactions follow WCAG 2.0 keyboard guidelines; each component documents its keyboard model.

### Accessibility as spec vocabulary
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/spec/
The Design Data Spec defines an **Accessibility vocabulary** per component — `role`, `intents`, `focusable`, `keyboardIntents`, `wcag`, and state-level AT fields (rules SPEC-030/031) — plus **informative platform adapter contracts** mapping foundation a11y vocabulary to **Web/ARIA, iOS UIAccessibility, Android AccessibilityNodeInfo, and voice/multimodal** surfaces.

### Implementation
**React Aria / React Spectrum** deliver WCAG-grade keyboard and screen-reader behavior; Spectrum Web Components CI runs aXe-core against ~50+ WCAG 2.0/2.1 A/AA rules (contrast, keyboard, ARIA, focus).

### Known gaps
- Color contrast is enforced via WCAG criteria and testing rather than a distinct "high-contrast" token context in the current published token set.
sections.dosdonts:
### Do's and Don'ts
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/spec/

Spectrum expresses correct usage as **executable conformance**, not only prose. The **Design Data Specification** validates in three layers (all under `@adobe/design-data-spec`):

| Layer | Artifact | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structural | `schemas/*.json` (JSON Schema Draft 2020-12) | Per-instance shape |
| Semantic | `rules/rules.yaml` | Rules with stable IDs (e.g. `SPEC-001`) |
| Fixtures | `conformance/` | Pass/fail conformance examples |

### Prose do/don'ts
Guideline documents attach typed **`do-dont` document blocks** to entities, so do's/don'ts are captured in the machine-readable guideline set alongside `purpose`, `guideline`, and `examples` blocks.

### Tooling
`design-data validate` and `design-data diff` check usage mechanically; semantic diff tracks token identity and property-level changes across dataset versions.

### Known gaps
- Spec is **Draft (v1.0.0-draft)**; rule IDs and schemas may change before 1.0.0.
sections.agent:
### Agent Guidance
> Source: https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-design-data/ai/

Spectrum Design Data ships first-party **MCP servers** and **Agent Skills** so assistants (Claude Code, Cursor) can query tokens, schemas, and S2 docs directly. Every capability comes as a **lightweight Agent Skill** (recommended for prototyping) and an **always-on MCP server**.

### MCP servers
- **`@adobe/design-data-mcp`** — Spectrum tokens + component schemas via the `@adobe/design-data` CLI, **zero-config embedded Spectrum snapshot**. Tools: `design-data-primer`, `design-data-query`, `design-data-suggest`, `design-data-component`, `design-data-resolve`.
- **`@adobe/design-data-agent-mcp`** — spec-conformant surface for any local dataset (`DESIGN_DATA_PATH`). Tools: `primer`, `resolve_token`, `query_tokens`, `describe_component`, `validate_usage`, `diff_datasets`, `write`, plus authoring-session tools.
- **Legacy `@adobe/spectrum-design-data-mcp`** — superseded by `@adobe/design-data-mcp`.

### Agent Skills
- **`design-data`** (Spectrum tokens, zero config), **`design-data-agent`** (spec/custom datasets), **`s2-docs`** (S2 component docs & guidelines).
- Install via `/plugin marketplace add adobe/spectrum-design-data` + `/plugin install …`, or a Cursor **Remote Rule (GitHub)** pointing at the skill folder. Skill descriptions load into context; tools shell out to the CLI on invoke.

### Delivery
- **`llms.txt`** + auto-generated markdown for the docs site.
- Skill and MCP can run together (skill = lightweight companion, MCP = full integration).

### Known gaps
- The DTCG-aligned dataset format is the spec's target; current `@adobe/spectrum-tokens` JSON remains the legacy shape during migration.
